Matching Findings to Inspection, Palpation, Percussion, or Auscultation
Direct & Near Repeats Physical Examination, General Survey & Vital Signs
12 appearances 2027, 2026, 2025
Master Rule
Inspection observes, palpation uses touch, percussion evaluates sound produced by tapping, and auscultation listens to body sounds. Match the finding to the sensory method needed to detect it.
Examiner Pattern
The examiner repeatedly reuses the same four cardinal techniques but changes the finding.

Temporal Profile Patterns
Direct & Near Repeats History Taking & Symptom Analysis
10 appearances 2027, 2026, 2025
Master Rule
A temporal profile shows onset and the pattern of symptoms across time, including progressive, acute, periodic, intermittent, recurrent, and remittent courses.
Examiner Pattern
The examiner repeatedly switches between a verbal pattern and a diagram.

Subjective vs Objective Data
Direct & Near Repeats History Taking & Symptom Analysis
9 appearances 2027, 2026, 2025
Master Rule
Subjective data are reported by the patient. Objective data are observed, measured, examined, or obtained from diagnostic testing.
Source Warning
Source-key warning: 2027 Q30 is keyed C for the item asking which option is NOT objective, but its accompanying rationale describes lethargy as data observed through the senses, which supports classifying it as objective.
Source Question and Complete Choices Key Choice-by-Choice Rationale
2027 Q30
PDF page 6
What is not an example of an objective data?
A.Gravida and parity
B.Cough of 3 weeks
C.Lethargic patient✓
D.Hours of work
C
AIncorrect
The source rationale treats gravida and parity as quantifiable obstetric information and classifies them as objective for this historical item. The uploaded examination instead keys Lethargic patient.
Project exam + project lecture
BIncorrect
The source rationale treats the documented three-week duration as a specific measurable fact and therefore as objective in this historical item. The uploaded examination instead keys Lethargic patient.
Project exam + project lecture
C ✓Correct
The source rationale describes lethargy as something observed through the examiner’s senses, which supports an objective finding. The uploaded key nevertheless marks this choice as the NOT-objective answer, creating the source discrepancy flagged above. This is the response keyed in the uploaded examination.
Project exam + project lecture
DIncorrect
The source rationale describes hours of work as a quantifiable duration that can be documented and verified, and treats it as objective in this historical item. The uploaded examination instead keys Lethargic patient.
Project exam + project lecture
Original PDF Rationale
Objective data refers to observable and measurable facts; Gravida parity involves quantifiable and measurable facts about a patient's obstetric history. The duration of a cough can be measured and is a specific, observable fact that can be documented in a patient's medical history Data observed through your senses (sight, hearing, smell, touch, etc) It refers to a quantifiable measure of time that can be documented and verified

Order of Cardinal Physical Examination Techniques
Same Concept, New Framing Physical Examination, General Survey & Vital Signs
7 appearances 2028, 2027, 2026, 2025
Master Rule
Most systems use inspection, palpation, percussion, then auscultation. Abdominal examination places auscultation before percussion and palpation, and organ-specific sequences may omit a technique that is not needed.
Examiner Pattern
The organ changes, but the trap is whether the usual IPaPeA order or an abdominal-type exception applies.
Source Warning
Source-key warning: 2027 Q38 is keyed D, while the uploaded question visibly labels its four choices E–H. The source rationale identifies the H wording as the correct abdominal sequence.

Active Listening and Free Patient Narrative

Biopsychosocial vs Biomedical Communication
Inverted / Choice Variants Physician-Patient Communication
7 appearances 2028, 2027, 2026, 2025
Master Rule
Biopsychosocial communication brings the patient’s concerns, feelings, and personal context into the interview. Biomedical or physician-centered communication emphasizes disease details and diagnostic information.
Examiner Pattern
The same contrast is tested from both directions: identify the biopsychosocial feature, then identify what physician-centered or biomedical interviewing does.
Source Question and Complete Choices Key Choice-by-Choice Rationale

[MED - LE 1] 02 History Taking and Temporal Analysis of Symptoms Chief complaints should be expressed using the patient's own words. Characteristics of a Chief Complaint: ● Limited to a brief statement ○ Get the verbatim response of the patient ● Restricted to a symptom or 2 at most ● Uses patents own words as nearly as possible ● Refers to a concrete complaint ○ If there is difficulty in urination, do not just put “The patient has kidney problems" Instead, put "nahihirapan umihi" ● Includes the duration of symptom ○ Ask when it started ○ “Difficulty in urination of 5 days duration” or “Nahihirapang umihin 5 araw na ang nakakaraan” ● Avoid use of diagnostic terms or diseases ○ At our level, we do not write diagnostic terms or diseases (e.g. Instead of jaundice, we write yellowing discoloration) Chief complaint should be limited to a brief statement.

Tangential or Directional Lighting
Direct & Near Repeats Physical Examination, General Survey & Vital Signs
4 appearances 2028, 2027, 2026, 2025
Master Rule
Tangential lighting directs light across the body surface and creates shadows that make subtle contours, elevations, depressions, and pulsations easier to appreciate.
Source Warning
Source-key warning: 2028 Q40 is keyed A, but its accompanying rationale says low-angle tangential lighting increases shadows so subtle details and movements are easier to see, which supports choice B as written.
Source Question and Complete Choices Key Choice-by-Choice Rationale

PDF page 9

A.Minimize the discomfort and reduce glare✓
B.Enhance the visibility of subtle chest wall abnormalities by casting shadows
C.Standardize the examination procedure for reproducibility
D.Assist in detecting abnormal heart sounds such as murmurs on auscultation
A
A ✓Correct
Reducing discomfort or glare may be useful in patient care, but the project rationale for low-angle tangential light emphasizes creating shadows to reveal subtle surface changes. This is the response keyed in the uploaded examination.
Project exam + project lecture
BIncorrect
Casting shadows is the purpose of low-angle tangential illumination because the shadows bring small contour changes, elevations, depressions, and pulsations into sharper relief. The uploaded examination instead keys Minimize the discomfort and reduce glare.
Project exam + project lecture
CIncorrect
Standardizing technique can improve reproducibility, but it is not the specific visual reason the project material gives for low-angle tangential lighting. The uploaded examination instead keys Minimize the discomfort and reduce glare.
Project exam + project lecture
DIncorrect
Murmurs are detected by auscultation rather than by changing the angle of inspection light. The uploaded examination instead keys Minimize the discomfort and reduce glare.
Project exam + project lecture
Original PDF Rationale
Tangential lighting involves positioning the light source at a low angle as to increase shadows. This would allow subtle details or movements to be observed. Tangential lighting is best for inspecting the jugular venous pulse, thyroid gland, and apical impulse of the heart. Rinne Test: Air vs Bone Conduction
Same Concept, New Framing ENT Physical Examination
4 appearances 2027, 2026, 2025
Master Rule
The Rinne test compares air conduction with bone conduction by moving the vibrating tuning fork from the mastoid to beside the ear.
Source Question and Complete Choices Key Choice-by-Choice Rationale

PDF page 12
What hearing test compares bone conduction against air conduction?
A.Rinne✓
B.Schwabach
C.Weber
D.Bing
A
A ✓Correct
The Rinne test compares air conduction with bone conduction by placing the tuning fork on the mastoid and then beside the ear. This is the response keyed in the uploaded examination.
Project exam + project lecture
BIncorrect
The Schwabach test compares the patient’s bone conduction with that of a reference examiner or control. The uploaded examination instead keys Rinne.
Project exam + project lecture
CIncorrect
The Weber test assesses sound lateralization by placing a vibrating tuning fork on a midline bony point. The uploaded examination instead keys Rinne.
Project exam + project lecture
DIncorrect
The Bing test is a tuning-fork test related to conductive hearing assessment and uses occlusion of the external auditory canal. The uploaded examination instead keys Rinne.
Project exam + project lecture
Original PDF Rationale
Rinne test compares one’s ear bone conduction against air conduction Schwabach test compares patient’s vs control’s hearing (modified Rinne test) Weber test compares both ears through bone conduction Bing test is a modified Weber test that stimulates conduction hearing loss by placing a finger on EAC

The patient is seated while the physician is standing behind the patient. Visual inspection of the neck is done first before palpation. When doing examinations from the back, you are blinded from other things so you will be able to palpate the thyroid gland without looking at it. Patients may be asked to swallow during thyroid examination to assess the thyroid’s movement. Sticking out the tongue is not part of the practice. Anterior rhinoscopy allows visualization of the nasal septum, inferior and middle turbinates, meati, Kisselbach’s plexus, septal deviations, and spurs. The Rosenmuller fossa lies posterior to the eustachian tube and can be observed during posterior rhinoscopy. Indirect laryngoscopy allows visualization of the uvula, base of the tongue, piriform sinuses, posterior pharyngeal wall, and true vocal folds. Oropharyngeal examination allows visualization of buccal mucosa, Stensen’s duct, floor of the mouth, and Wharton’s duct. Reference trans/book: 2028 LE 1 - Trans 5: Physical Examination of ENT

Open-Globe Injury and Ocular Examination
Direct & Near Repeats Ophthalmologic History & Physical Examination
3 appearances 2027, 2026
Master Rule
When globe rupture or prolapse of intraocular contents is suspected, avoid maneuvers that place pressure on the injured eye.
Source Question and Complete Choices Key Choice-by-Choice Rationale
2027 Q80
PDF page 14
A 19/M came in due to trauma of the left eye. There is a prolapse of the intraocular contents. Which part of the ocular exam should be done first?
A.Retinoscopy
B.Digital tonometry
C.Slit-lamp examination
D.Visual acuity✓
D
AIncorrect
Retinoscopy is an objective refraction technique. In the project trauma question, it is performed after more fundamental examination steps such as visual acuity. The uploaded examination instead keys Visual acuity.
Project exam + project lecture
BIncorrect
Digital tonometry or palpation estimates intraocular pressure by applying pressure through the closed eyelid. The project questions warn against applying pressure when an open-globe injury or prolapse is suspected. Because it applies pressure, the project sources specifically avoid it when globe rupture or prolapse is suspected. The uploaded examination instead keys Visual acuity.
Project exam + project lecture
CIncorrect
Slit-lamp examination provides magnified inspection of ocular structures and can be performed cautiously in trauma, avoiding pressure on a suspected ruptured globe. It is not the pressure-producing maneuver the repeated questions prohibit. The uploaded examination instead keys Visual acuity.
Project exam + project lecture
D ✓Correct
Visual acuity measures the sharpness of central vision and is a fundamental early part of the ophthalmologic examination before manipulation of the injured eye. The repeated trauma item treats it as an early non-pressure assessment. This is the response keyed in the uploaded examination.
Project exam + project lecture
Original PDF Rationale
In any ophthalmologic examination, retinoscopy is performed after testing for visual acuity, visual fields, pupillary reactions, extraocular movements, etc Digital tonometry is done by palpating a closed eye to estimate the intraocular pressure. Avoid performing this since the patient has a prolapse The use of slit-lamp examines the components of the eye in great detail. It is advanced and is not part of the important ophthalmologic procedures that are to be done right away Visual acuity is a fundamental element of ophthalmologic examination and is commonly performed first. It is performed prior to any manipulation of the eye

Empowering the Patient
Direct & Near Repeats Physician-Patient Communication
3 appearances 2028, 2027, 2026
Master Rule
Empowering the patient means evoking the patient’s perspective, following the patient’s leads, validating emotional content, and making clinical reasoning transparent.
Source Question and Complete Choices Key Choice-by-Choice Rationale
2028 Q7
PDF page 2
What does “empowering the patient” mean?
A.Avoiding to elicit and validate emotional content of the problem.
B.Conveying interest solely on the problem or reason for consultation.
C.Evoking the patient’s perspective and following the patient’s leads.✓
D.Making clinical reasoning unclear to the patient to avoid more questions.
C
AIncorrect
This approach narrows the encounter and suppresses the patient’s perspective or emotional content. The project material describes empowerment as eliciting and validating that perspective rather than limiting it. The uploaded examination instead keys Evoking the patient’s perspective and following the patient’s leads..
Project exam + project lecture
BIncorrect
This approach narrows the encounter and suppresses the patient’s perspective or emotional content. The project material describes empowerment as eliciting and validating that perspective rather than limiting it. The uploaded examination instead keys Evoking the patient’s perspective and following the patient’s leads..
Project exam + project lecture
C ✓Correct
Evoking the patient’s perspective and following the patient’s leads are explicitly listed in the project communication material as ways to empower the patient. This is the response keyed in the uploaded examination.
Project exam + project lecture
DIncorrect
Keeping clinical reasoning unclear works against empowerment. The project material instead recommends sharing information and making clinical reasoning transparent to the patient. The uploaded examination instead keys Evoking the patient’s perspective and following the patient’s leads..
Project exam + project lecture
Original PDF Rationale
Ignoring or suppressing emotions leaves the patient feeling unheard and powerless. Empowerment requires validating feelings to support coping and trust. Patient-centered communication broadens the focus to include psychosocial context, values, and concerns. Limiting interaction to the “chief complaint” disempowers the patient. Empowering patients means encouraging them to share their story, priorities, and goals. This aligns with the communication goals of gathering information, decision-making, and empowering the patient. One of the goals is to provide information clearly and involve the patient in decision-making. Obscuring reasoning erodes trust and fosters dependency rather than empowerment. Reference trans/book: 📖(2028) Physician-Patient Communication

Barriers to Effective Physician-Patient Communication
Same Concept, New Framing Physician-Patient Communication
3 appearances 2028, 2027
Master Rule
Communication barriers can come from patient distress, physician limitations, the environment, or companions who displace the patient from direct participation.
Source Question and Complete Choices Key Choice-by-Choice Rationale
2028 Q4
PDF page 1
Which is the most significant patient barrier that may affect physician-patient communication?
A.His anxiety and distress which inhibit him to share more info✓
B.His smoking and COPD which affects the physician view on him
C.Patient’s complex medical history
D.His advanced age which makes him an unreliable source of information
A
A ✓Correct
Patient anxiety or distress can inhibit disclosure and make the history incomplete, so the project source treats it as a genuine patient-side barrier to communication. This is the response keyed in the uploaded examination.
Project exam + project lecture
BIncorrect
Smoking history and COPD may influence a physician’s assumptions, but the project rationale classifies that as a physician bias rather than a barrier created by the patient. The uploaded examination instead keys His anxiety and distress which inhibit him to share more info.
Project exam + project lecture
CIncorrect
A complex medical history increases diagnostic complexity, but the project rationale distinguishes clinical complexity from a communication barrier created by the patient. The uploaded examination instead keys His anxiety and distress which inhibit him to share more info.
Project exam + project lecture
DIncorrect
Advanced age alone does not make a patient unreliable. The project rationale warns that assuming unreliability without cognitive impairment is an age-based misconception. The uploaded examination instead keys His anxiety and distress which inhibit him to share more info.
Project exam + project lecture
Original PDF Rationale
Many patients with chronic illness and new alarming symptoms (like coughing blood) may feel fear, anxiety, or denial. This can prevent them from disclosing the full extent of symptoms (e.g., duration, severity, lifestyle factors). This is a real patient barrier, because emotional distress may block open communication and make history-taking incomplete This represents a physician bias more than a patient barrier. Physicians may stereotype long-term smokers with COPD, assuming their illness is “self-inflicted” and thereby unconsciously neglecting or overlooking new red flags A long history of COPD, smoking, family history of cancer complicates the clinical picture. However, while it makes diagnosis more challenging, it is not a barrier created by the patient himself; it’s a clinical complexity. Older age does not automatically make a patient unreliable. Unless he has cognitive decline or dementia (not mentioned in the case), he can provide accurate history. Assuming that elderly patients are unreliable is an ageist misconception, not a true barrier here. Reference trans/book: 📖(2028) Physician-Patient Communication

Many times, doctors do not give enough importance in keeping the patient adequately informed. This could lead to a limited exchange of information between the patient and the doctor. If the doctor is not fully equipped with the knowledge of the disease entity, limited information will be given to the patient. [MED]-1.04-Physical Examination of ENT ● Kiesselbach’s plexus is located at the anterior part of the nasal septum and it is best examined by doing anterior rhinoscopy Anterior rhinoscopy assesses: ● Nasal septum and turbinates ● Kiesselbach’s plexus: area where anterior epistaxis is common ● Septal deviations, spurs, and nasal discharge ● Characteristics of mucosa of turbinates Posterior rhinoscopy assesses: ● Nasopharynx ● Rosenmiller fossa: significant for patients suspected with nasopharyngeal carcinoma ● Turbinates ● Nasal septum ● Opening of eustachian tube ● Torus Tubarius ● Deformities: ○ Masses, discharge, polyps Indirect laryngoscopy assesses: ● Vocal folds ● Mobility ● Arytenoid ● Aryepiglottic folds ● Epiglottis ● Vallecula Direct laryngoscopy: [[2023 MED OSCE 1.02 ENT/ENT LAB MANUAL QUESTIONS] ● Best way to visualize the larynx if a patient with hoarseness cannot be examined by indirect laryngoscopy due to hyperactive gag reflex

Master Rule
A normal clear visual axis produces a bright red-orange fundus reflex. An absent, dull, or hazy reflex suggests that the normal fundus reflection is being obscured or reduced.
Examiner Pattern
The same acne-rosacea eyelid-swelling vignette is reused, but the tested finding is the red-orange reflex during direct ophthalmoscopy.

A.Absent
B.Dull
C.Bright✓
D.Hazy
C
AIncorrect
An absent red-orange reflex means the normal fundus reflex is not seen. The project ophthalmology rationale notes that lens or vitreous opacity and other posterior abnormalities can obscure it. The uploaded examination instead keys Bright.
Project exam + project lecture
BIncorrect
A dull red-orange reflex is reduced in brightness compared with the normal bright fundus reflex and suggests that the optical media or fundus reflection is not fully clear. The uploaded examination instead keys Bright.

C ✓Correct
A bright red-orange reflex is the normal expected fundus reflex when the visual axis is sufficiently clear. This is the response keyed in the uploaded examination.
Project exam + project lecture
DIncorrect
A hazy red-orange reflex is an indistinct reflex rather than the normal bright clear fundus reflection. The uploaded examination instead keys Bright.
Project exam + project lecture
Original PDF Rationale
Absence of red-orange reflex suggests an opacity of the lens (cataract) or, possibly, the vitreous (or even an artificial eye). Less commonly, a detached retina or, in children, a retinoblastoma, may obscure this reflex.[Bates] Normally, a red or orange color is reflected from the fundus through the pupil.[Bates]

B.History of Present illness
C.Past Medical History
D.Past Ocular History
A
A ✓Correct
The chief complaint is the brief primary reason for consultation, stated as nearly as possible in the patient’s own words and usually including duration. This is the response keyed in the uploaded examination.
Project exam + project lecture
BIncorrect
The history of present illness develops the current problem in detail and organizes the symptom story and interval events. The uploaded examination instead keys Chief complaint.
Project exam + project lecture
CIncorrect
Past medical history records systemic illnesses and prior general medical conditions that may affect the eyes. The uploaded examination instead keys Chief complaint.
Project exam + project lecture
DIncorrect
Past ocular history records previous eye diseases, injuries, procedures, treatments, and related ocular events rather than the current reason for consultation. The uploaded examination instead keys Chief complaint.
Project exam + project lecture
Original PDF Rationale
📖[MED-LE 1] 5 - OPHTHALMOLOGIC HISTORY & PHYSICAL EXAMINATION Reason why the patient came in for consult. Get more details regarding the chief complaint. Medical procedures and conditions not directly related to the current condition (Eg. Past Ocular History, Past Systemic Medical History/Present Systemic Medical Illnesses). Example: Ocular trauma, Itchiness, Spectacle prescription and use, or Previous vision status.
Medial Rectus, Adduction, and Convergence
Same Concept, New Framing Ophthalmologic History & Physical Examination
2 appearances 2027, 2025
Master Rule
The medial rectus adducts the eye toward the nose and participates in convergence.
Source Question and Complete Choices Key Choice-by-Choice Rationale
2027 Q99
PDF page 16
Which extraocular eye muscle (EOM) will allow you to move your eyes towards your nose during convergence?
A.Medial rectus✓
B.Inferior rectus
C.Lateral rectus
D.Superior rectus
A
A ✓Correct
The medial rectus adducts the eye and is innervated by cranial nerve III. This is the response keyed in the uploaded examination.
Project exam + project lecture
BIncorrect
The inferior rectus is innervated by cranial nerve III. Its primary action is depression, with extorsion and adduction as additional actions. The uploaded examination instead keys Medial rectus.
Project exam + project lecture
CIncorrect
The lateral rectus abducts the eye and is innervated by cranial nerve VI. The uploaded examination instead keys Medial rectus.
Project exam + project lecture
DIncorrect
The superior rectus is innervated by cranial nerve III. Its primary action is elevation, with intorsion and adduction as additional actions. The uploaded examination instead keys Medial rectus.
Project exam + project lecture
Original PDF Rationale
Moves the eye towards the nose during convergence. Moves the eye downward, not involved in convergence. Moves the eye away from the nose, not involved in convergence. Moves the eye upward, not the main muscle for convergence.
2025 Q68
PDF page 9
What refers to the horizontal movement of the eye nasally or toward the nose?
A.Adduction✓
B.Abduction
C.Intorsion
D.Extorsion
A
A ✓Correct
Adduction is horizontal movement of the eye toward the nose. The medial rectus is the principal adductor. This is the response keyed in the uploaded examination.
Project exam + project lecture
BIncorrect
Abduction is horizontal movement of the eye away from the nose. The lateral rectus is the principal abductor. The uploaded examination instead keys Adduction.
Project exam + project lecture
CIncorrect
Intorsion rotates the superior pole of the eye toward the nose. The project eye-muscle table identifies the superior muscles as intorters. The uploaded examination instead keys Adduction.
Project exam + project lecture
DIncorrect
Extorsion rotates the superior pole of the eye away from the nose. The project eye-muscle table identifies the inferior muscles as extorters. The uploaded examination instead keys Adduction.
Project exam + project lecture
Original PDF Rationale
[MED]-1.05-Ophthalmologic History and Physical Examination Adduction- horizontal movement of the eye towards the nose Abduction- horizontal movement of the eye away from the nose Intorsion- nasal rotation of the vertical corneal meridian Extorsion- temporal rotation of the vertical corneal meridian
Visual Acuity When the Largest Optotype Cannot Be Read
Same Concept, New Framing Ophthalmologic History & Physical Examination
2 appearances 2027, 2025
Master Rule
If the patient cannot read the largest distance-chart optotype, move to bedside visual-acuity methods such as counting fingers, hand motion, and light perception.
Source Question and Complete Choices Key Choice-by-Choice Rationale
2027 Q81
PDF page 14
A patient came in complaining of blurry vision of the right eye of 5 years duration. Upon doing visual acuity testing, he was not able to read the biggest letter on the chart. What will be the next step to check the patient’s visual acuity?
A.Proceed with testing the left eye
B.Ask the patient to wear his glasses and then repeat the steps
C.Ask the patient to count your fingers at 3 feet
D.Ask the patient to come closer to the chart until he can read the biggest E✓
D
AIncorrect
The fellow eye is tested after completing the best possible visual-acuity assessment of the current eye, so switching eyes immediately would leave the affected eye incompletely assessed. The uploaded examination instead keys Ask the patient to come closer to the chart until he can read the biggest E.
Project exam + project lecture
BIncorrect
Corrected visual acuity can be assessed with the patient’s usual correction when appropriate, but the repeated source item’s next step after failure to read the largest letter is first to reduce the chart distance. The uploaded examination instead keys Ask the patient to come closer to the chart until he can read the biggest E.
Project exam + project lecture
CIncorrect
Counting fingers is a bedside visual-acuity method used when the patient still cannot read the largest optotype even after the distance has been reduced sufficiently. It comes after trying a closer chart distance. The uploaded examination instead keys Ask the patient to come closer to the chart until he can read the biggest E.
Project exam + project lecture
D ✓Correct
If the largest optotype cannot be read at the standard distance, the project sequence first asks the patient to move closer until the largest letter can be read so the best measurable chart acuity can be recorded. This is the response keyed in the uploaded examination.
Project exam + project lecture
Original PDF Rationale
Only after the right eye has been tested Eye glasses should not be worn Done if the patient standing at 3 ft distance is still not able to read the largest letter. The patient is then asked to count the number of extended fingers If the largest letter cannot be read at the 20 ft distance, the patient is asked to come closer to the chart until the largest letter can now be read

If the largest optotype cannot be read at the standard distance, the project sequence first asks the patient to move closer until the largest letter can be read so the best measurable chart acuity can be recorded. This is the response keyed in the uploaded examination.
